tools.name: list_pay_apps
tools.description: List your independent Pay applications. No development project required. Paginated: nextCursor is set while more results exist. Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: create_pay_app
tools.description: Create an independent Pay application; linking a development project is optional. `trialDays` (0–365, optional) sets a free trial at once, since a new application has no buyers yet; set_pay_trial changes it later. Not idempotent: each call creates a new application, including a call repeated after a timeout. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: get_pay_app
tools.description: Read your Pay application, its optional project link and its free trial (`trialDays`, null when there is none). Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: get_pay_readiness
tools.description: Check current checkout and launch prerequisites. A passing checkout check does not prove a live external purchase or SDK publication. `warnings` are non-blocking (`ready` ignores them): offer_translations lists offer text not yet translated into the project's languages, with counts per language and fixWith (get_pay_offer_translations → set_pay_offer_translations). Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: get_pay_payment_evidence
tools.description: Read what Extenshi's own payment ledger proves about this application's payment path, per mode: checkout completed, license issued, an installation received the signed license, restored on a second installation, refund revoked. Derived from provider-signed webhooks, not from any report; opaque IDs and timestamps only, no buyer data. Only a live-mode purchase can satisfy a release's payment requirement; test-mode purchases are listed without satisfying it. Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: link_pay_app
tools.description: Link your Pay application to your development project. Existing purchases remain attached to the Pay application. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: unlink_pay_app
tools.description: Remove the optional development-project link without deleting Pay data. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: archive_pay_app
tools.description: Archive your application and stop new checkout. Payment records and existing entitlements are preserved. With this connection’s API key the change applies at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) turns it into a proposal. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: export_pay_data
tools.description: Export one page of one resource (offers, payments, subscriptions, entitlements or customers). nextCursor is null on the last page. Offer rows include sortOrder, their position on the paywall (lower shows first). The output contains sensitive customer and payment data. Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: get_pay_seller
tools.description: Read seller connection, public profile, offers (terms, sortOrder, active and sync state), the publishable SDK key and the public entitlement verification key. Those two keys are the ones meant to be embedded in extension code; secret keys are not part of the response. Agreement signing and KYC take place in the browser. Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: connect_pay_seller
tools.description: Start Stripe Connect onboarding and return a browser action URL. KYC and legal acceptance are completed by the author at that URL; this tool does not perform them. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: refresh_pay_seller
tools.description: Refresh current payment-provider onboarding status. This does not complete KYC or accept agreements. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: set_pay_seller_profile
tools.description: Save the public seller profile: display name, support URL or email, and terms URL. The values are stored as provided and are publicly visible. With this connection’s API key the change applies at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) turns it into a proposal. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: upsert_pay_offer
tools.description: Create or update an offer keyed by a stable SKU. On an existing offer every omitted field keeps its stored value: to change only the title or description, send appId, sku and the new text, and the price, features and paywall order (sortOrder) stay as they are; `description: null` clears the description. A new SKU needs kind, amountMinor, currency and title (and interval for a subscription), with sortOrder 0 when omitted (lower shows first). An archived SKU needs the same, since saving it puts it back on sale. Price is in minor currency units. Subscriptions keep the given billing interval; one-time and lifetime offers store no interval. Price and features are stored as provided. `features` are entitlement keys (e.g. `full`): the SDK checks them with hasFeature and extensions match offers by them, so they stay untranslated; localized paywall bullets come from the extension, via showPaywall({ features }) with text from its _locales. `followUps` names the translations a changed title or description left missing or outdated (set_pay_offer_translations). With this connection’s API key the change applies at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) turns it into a proposal. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: archive_pay_offer
tools.description: Stop offering a SKU for new checkout; historical purchases are preserved. With this connection’s API key the change applies at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) turns it into a proposal. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: get_pay_offer_translations
tools.description: Read the translatable text of the application's active offers (title, description) keyed `<sku>/<field>`, with the project's languages and each language's translated, missing and outdated fields. Feature keys are entitlement keys, listed under `notTranslated` and not counted as missing. The paywall shows an offer in the buyer's browser language when the project ships it; the SDK's own buttons and labels are already translated. get_project_state `localization` summarizes this with every other translated surface. Requires pay.read permission.

tools.name: set_pay_offer_translations
tools.description: Save one language of the offers' translations: `translations` maps `<sku>/<field>` keys from get_pay_offer_translations to text; `sources` (optional) carries the original each was translated from, and a save whose original has changed since is refused. An empty string removes a translation; a `<sku>/feature:<n>` key is refused (TRANSLATIONS_INVALID: features are entitlement keys). Prices, SKUs, plans and feature keys are not changed. Answers with the saved language's translations and every language's status (`view: 'saved_locale'`, the default); `view: 'all_locales'` returns every language's translations, as get_pay_offer_translations does. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: set_pay_enabled
tools.description: Enable or disable new payments for the application; requires a connected payment provider. Enabling re-reads the seller status from the provider (charges and payouts). It does not verify the public profile, agreement or offer sync: buyers can check out only when every readiness check reported by get_pay_readiness passes. Enabling is a live commerce change. With this connection’s API key the change applies at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) turns it into a proposal. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: set_pay_trial
tools.description: Set the application's free trial: `trialDays` (0–365) free days for every installation, counted on Extenshi's server from the first time the SDK reads that installation's license; null turns the trial off. One clock per installation per application, so switching offers does not restart it, and an installation restored through purchase recovery keeps the earliest start. The end is derived from the stored start, so a new length also moves trials already running. The SDK reads it with getTrial() and the trial:ending / trial:ended events; the extension does not store a start date itself. With this connection’s API key the change applies at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) turns it into a proposal. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: rotate_pay_key
tools.description: Generate a new publishable SDK key. Not idempotent: each call issues another key. Prior keys remain accepted for installed extension builds; this does not revoke any secret. Requires pay.write permission.

tools.name: import_manifest
tools.description: Import an existing manifest.json into the Dojo manifest editor and project labels. Input: parsed JSON, optional default-locale messages, and optional messagesByLocale — every _locales/<lang>/messages.json keyed by locale code (only the keys named by the __MSG_*__ fields of the manifest are needed) — whose non-default locales fill the Dojo translations of name and description. Repository translations replace editor text per field; translations the repository lacks are kept, and warnings name each replaced one. Source import fills supported fields and preserves all other JSON; built imports remain separate observations. Default dryRun=true returns changes and expectedStateHash without writing; dryRun=false with that hash applies them. Does not infer data collection, prices, or publication. Requires project.write. `provenance` is required: {source: "agent", observedAt: ISO-8601 timestamp, toolVersion: your client name and version}.

messagesByLocale.description: Messages per _locales/<lang> folder, keyed by locale code (en, pt_BR, …). Non-default locales fill the Dojo translations of name and description; the default locale stands in for messages when that is omitted. Only the keys the manifest references are needed.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new extension project (a Dojo workspace) owned by this identity, through the same service the Dojo project wizard uses, with the same ownership and limits. Returns JSON {projectId, dojoUrl, project, pendingDecisions, nextSteps}: the next steps cover binding the repository and the starter files. Idempotent: a repeated request with the same idempotencyKey returns the project it already created (replayed: true); the same key with different input is rejected. Requires project.write. On this local server the answer also carries `buildMap` {running, url (while running), offered, declined, offers, home} for projectDir: the author’s build map (npx @extenshi/cli map), one per project for every agent and git worktree; absent when the directory cannot be read.

projectDir.description: The extension project's directory on this machine, absolute or relative to this server's working directory (default: the working directory). In a linked git worktree, buildMap describes the map of the main checkout, which every agent and worktree of the project shares.

tools.name: get_decisions
tools.description: Owner decisions for one project: the AMO add-on id, license, seller public name, support contact and terms, pricing, target browsers and target locales. Each entry reports its status (undecided, proposed or decided), the value, a suggested default where one is derivable (a stable {GUID} add-on id or the id already in the Firefox manifest, the project browsers), who proposed or decided it and when, and which releases it blocks (blocksBrowsers, blocksPayment). `pending` lists the keys the owner has not decided. FREE.

tools.name: propose_decision
tools.description: Propose a value for one owner decision. The proposal is stored with its rationale, proposer and time; the owner accepts or edits it on the Dojo project page, which is the only place a decision becomes decided. A key the owner already decided is refused (DECISION_ALREADY_DECIDED). Value formats: amo.addonId {GUID} or name@domain; license an AMO license slug (below); seller.publicName text; seller.supportContact an email or HTTPS URL; seller.terms an HTTPS URL; pricing {model: free|paid|donations, trialDays?, plans?: subscription|lifetime|one_time}; targetBrowsers an array of chrome/firefox/edge; targetLocales an array of locale codes. License: AMO accepts exactly these case-sensitive slugs: all-rights-reserved, MIT, Apache-2.0, MPL-2.0, GPL-3.0-only, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, GPL-2.0-only, LGPL-2.1-only, LGPL-3.0-only, AGPL-3.0-only, Unlicense. Another SPDX id (BSD-3-Clause, GPL-3.0-or-later) is accepted, but AMO then needs it as customLicense (name + text) in the listing. npm's UNLICENSED in package.json means proprietary, so propose all-rights-reserved; Unlicense is a public-domain dedication. A misspelled slug (mit, GPL-3.0, UNLICENSED) is refused. Idempotent per idempotencyKey. Requires project.write.

proposedBy.description: Agent or tool label recorded with the proposal.

tools.name: set_store_listing
tools.description: Record where this project is listed in one store and how far it got: status planned (not submitted), submitted (sent for review, in review) or live (public). Works before the listing is public: an AMO URL in review, a Chrome item id reserved in the Developer Dashboard, an Edge Partner Center productId before any public URL exists. url is that store's listing page (chromewebstore.google.com/detail/…, addons.mozilla.org/…/addon/<slug>/, microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/…); itemId is the public store id (Chrome 32 letters a–p, AMO slug/number/GUID, Edge 32 letters a–z); productId is Edge-only; submittedAt a date. A live listing needs url or itemId. The entry is replaced whole (fields you leave out are removed); listing null removes it. Only live listings reach public pages: draft_landing_page fills install buttons from them, not from planned or submitted ones. Read them back in get_project_state workspace.document.storeListings or list_my_projects. Returns {listings, urls, publicUrls, pending, revision}. Idempotent per idempotencyKey. Requires project.write.

tools.name: get_release_readiness
tools.description: Explain readiness for the recorded browser and artifact by locale. Local or agent reports are not treated as CI attestations. Stale evidence does not pass. Requires a Pro project. Readiness is measured against the release recorded in the workspace: until apply_project_patch sets patch.release (browser, version, artifactDigest, manifestDigest, locales, paymentRequired, and commit or dirtyTreeDigest) it reports RELEASE_NOT_RECORDED; after that, evidence counts only when it matches that release artifactDigest. When the project has a linked Pay application, the payment check also carries `platform`: what Extenshi's own payment ledger proves (checkout, license, installation activation, recovery, refund). A live-mode purchase through those stages passes the check with source 'platform'; test-mode purchases are listed without passing it. Clients cannot record source 'platform'. `warnings` lists what does not block but needs action before upload, such as a decided license that is not an AMO slug and needs customLicense in the AMO listing, and TRANSLATIONS_INCOMPLETE: server-side text (Pay offers, license terms, privacy policy, hosted pages, landing page) still missing or outdated in the project languages, each surface with its fixWith tools — the same counts as get_project_state `localization`.

tools.name: upsert_hosted_page
tools.description: Register the project's homepage or support page URL (HTTPS only; the server fetches the public page and hashes the body, so the URL has to be publicly reachable). The registered homepage URL feeds HOMEPAGE_URL when the integration config file is regenerated. Requires hosted.write. API reference: https://docs.extenshi.io/developers/project-sync#hosted-pages-from-the-api

tools.name: verify_hosted_artifact
tools.description: Verify a hosted page actually serves what its record says: re-fetches and compares content. kind=homepage|support compares against the registered body hash (verified | changed | unreachable); kind=privacy checks the published policy version's HTML is what the public page really serves. Requires hosted.write. API reference: https://docs.extenshi.io/developers/project-sync#hosted-pages-from-the-api

tools.name: remove_hosted_page
tools.description: Remove the project's registered homepage or support page — for a project moving off a URL or a mis-registered address. The public page itself keeps working; only the project record is forgotten. Requires hosted.write. API reference: https://docs.extenshi.io/developers/project-sync#hosted-pages-from-the-api

tools.name: publish_landing_page
tools.description: Publish the project's landing page (homepage) on Extenshi hosting — the same page generate_landing_page returns, rendered server-side from the form (no caller HTML is stored) and served at page.extenshi.io/{code}, or at the root of the project's custom domain once it is ACTIVE (set_custom_domain). A schema-v2 form (schemaVersion 2; draft_landing_page returns one, preview_landing_page validates it) adds sections, theme tokens, SEO, per-locale pages at {url}/{locale} with hreflang, and llms.txt; pricing plans with offerSku take price and period from the live Pay offer. The code is permanent: republishing creates a new version at the same URL. By default the URL is also registered as the project homepage, which feeds HOMEPAGE_URL. Hosted images are limited to store screenshot URLs (from get_extension) and images uploaded in the Dojo Page generator or with upload_project_media (use its url for local screenshots or a logo); the logo may also be an inline SVG or a raster data: URL. After publishing, the server fetches the public URL: live.status is verified (it serves these bytes), changed or unreachable (with live.detail, e.g. HTTP 404) — only verified means visitors see the page. Returns JSON {url, publicCode, versionNumber, contentHash, bytes, warnings, homepage, live, nextSteps, followUps}; followUps names project languages the form has no locales.<tag> page for. Requires hosted.write. API reference: https://docs.extenshi.io/developers/project-sync#hosted-pages-from-the-api

tools.name: draft_landing_page
tools.description: Draft a full homepage (schema v2) from what the project already knows: the manifest draft and its store translations, the published page or saved Page generator form, public project media, Extenshi Pay offers (pricing plans bound by SKU), hosted artifacts (privacy policy, uninstall feedback form, license terms), owner decisions (seller.supportContact for supportUrl, pricing for the trial in the FAQ), the newest source/built manifest version and the locales, with built-in headings translated for the languages Extenshi ships. Writes nothing. Returns JSON {form, sources (field → where it came from), todos (what only you can supply — features, how-it-works, real testimonials, translations), problems, previewUrl}. The form is accepted as-is by preview_landing_page and publish_landing_page. The install buttons come from the project's live store listings (set_store_listing); planned or submitted listings stay off the page and appear in todos instead. storeUrls overrides them for a store; accentColor sets the brand colour (the server cannot see your Pay SDK theme). Requires project.read.

storeUrls.description: Store listing URLs, when the project does not have them yet.

accentColor.description: Brand colour #rrggbb for the accent — e.g. theme.primaryColor of the Extenshi Pay SDK config in the extension.

tools.description: Validate and render a landing form exactly as publish_landing_page would — same image rules, store-locale check, Pay offer prices and canonical URL — without publishing. Requires project.read.

tools.name: verify_custom_domain

tools.name: remove_custom_domain

tools.description: Search the cross-store extension catalog (Chrome, Firefox, Edge). A free-text query matches the listing name and description, and also the features extracted for the extension (what it does). A result that matched through a feature lists it in `matchedFeatures`. Features are extracted for part of the catalog, so a result without `matchedFeatures` may still have the function. All filters (rating/reviews thresholds, store, category, pricing, risk, permissions, freshness, manifest version, trader status) are applied server-side by the catalog database, so a filtered request returns only the matching subset. `skip` pages through large result sets. Store-specific constraints (validated client-side, before any request): `minWeeklyDownloads` only applies to FIREFOX; combining it with a `stores` filter that excludes those stores is rejected. Returns a compact list for market research and competitive analysis.

query.description: Free-text search query: a name, keywords, or a function such as "picture in picture".

stores.description: Stores to search: CHROME, FIREFOX and/or EDGE.

minWeeklyDownloads.description: Minimum weekly downloads — FIREFOX-ONLY metric (not reported by Chrome/Edge). Chrome/Edge popularity is available through sortBy:"popular". A request combining it with a Chrome/Edge-only `stores` filter is rejected.

includeDelisted.description: Whether extensions whose store listing was removed are included (default: excluded).

sortBy.description: Sort field (default: popular, or relevance when a query is given).

tools.name: get_extension
tools.description: Get full catalog detail for one extension: metadata, per-store ratings, install counts, categories, and a security badge. Identify it by numeric catalog `extension_id` OR by its `store_id` (the id in the store URL; add `store` for a Chrome/Edge id).

store_id.description: Alternative to extension_id: the extension’s id in its store URL (e.g. Chrome "cjpalhdlnbpafiamejdnhcphjbkeiagm"). A Chrome/Edge id (32 letters a–p) also requires `store`: both stores share that format. Firefox ids (slug / GUID / email) are unambiguous. Resolving a store_id is free; only the read that follows costs a credit.

store.description: Which store `store_id` belongs to. REQUIRED for Chrome/Edge ids (identical format).

tools.name: get_reviews
tools.description: Get store user reviews for one extension from Firefox Add-ons and Edge Add-ons: star rating, a short review excerpt, date and language, plus a store-level `aggregate` (rating, count, reviews link). Chrome Web Store review rows are NOT returned (their text cannot be redistributed) — for a Chrome extension the `aggregate` (with a link to the store reviews tab) is the only public review content. Reviewer identity is intentionally omitted. Paginated newest-first by default (or by highest rating); `cursor` takes the `nextCursor` from a previous call. Cursors are sort-specific: a cursor is valid only with the `sort` it was issued for. Reads existing scraped reviews; `min_rating` narrows to positive or critical feedback.

store_id.description: Alternative to extension_id: the extension’s id in its store URL (e.g. Chrome "cjpalhdlnbpafiamejdnhcphjbkeiagm"). A Chrome/Edge id (32 letters a–p) also requires `store`: both stores share that format. Firefox ids (slug / GUID / email) are unambiguous. Resolving a store_id is free; only the read that follows costs a credit.

store.description: Which store `store_id` belongs to. REQUIRED for Chrome/Edge ids (identical format).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor: the `nextCursor` value returned by a previous call.

language_id.description: Only reviews in this catalog language id.

min_rating.description: Only reviews with a star rating ≥ this (1–5).

sort.description: Order by newest first (default) or highest rating.

tools.name: get_security
tools.description: Get the security analysis for an extension: safety score (0–100, higher = safer — the same coefficient the website shows), risk category, finding counts by severity, and the top grouped findings (scanner, rule, severity, count). Also returns an approximate install-dialog preview computed from the store-listed permissions (consolidated + deduped), available even for unscanned extensions. Reads existing scan results — does not trigger a new scan. Identify the extension by numeric `extension_id` OR `store_id` (+`store` for Chrome/Edge). NB: this tool costs 3 read credits (it fetches security, risk, and install-preview data).

store_id.description: Alternative to extension_id: the extension’s id in its store URL (e.g. Chrome "cjpalhdlnbpafiamejdnhcphjbkeiagm"). A Chrome/Edge id (32 letters a–p) also requires `store`: both stores share that format. Firefox ids (slug / GUID / email) are unambiguous. Resolving a store_id is free; only the read that follows costs a credit.

store.description: Which store `store_id` belongs to. REQUIRED for Chrome/Edge ids (identical format).

tools.name: get_risk_by_store_ids
tools.description: Look up the safety score and risk category for MANY extensions at once, addressed by their STORE ids (the id in the store URL) — the inventory case: you have a list of what a user has installed and need risk for all of it. Up to 40 extensions per call, and the WHOLE call costs 1 read credit (not 1 per extension; get_security costs 3 credits per extension). Returns safety score (0–100, higher = safer, the same number the website shows), risk category, severity counts, last scan date and the catalog URL per extension. Each store id is resolved through its cross-store cluster to the same listing the extension page renders, so these answers agree with the website. `store` is REQUIRED per entry — Chrome and Edge ids share one format. An extension with no score has not been scanned yet (`scanned: false`); ids with no catalog listing come back under `notInCatalog`. Neither means "safe". The full findings list of ONE extension comes from get_security.

store_id.description: The extension id from its store URL, e.g. "cjpalhdlnbpafiamejdnhcphjbkeiagm".

store.description: Which store this id belongs to. Required — Chrome and Edge ids look identical.

extensions.description: The extensions to look up (max 40). A longer list takes several calls of up to 40; each call costs 1 read credit.

annotations.title: Bulk risk lookup by store id

tools.name: market_overview
tools.description: Aggregate catalog market intelligence. Called with NO arguments it returns a full CATALOG-WIDE overview: totals, store split, the category tree, and the extended facet breakdown — Manifest V2/V3 adoption, sensitive-permission histogram, security risk-tier distribution, trader status, update-recency, and review-count buckets. Pass a `query` (and/or store/category filters) to scope those facets to a search result set instead.

query.description: Optional query to scope facets to a search.

facets.description: Facet groups to include: stats, stores, categories, extended, questionnaire, downloads; all groups when omitted.

top_n.description: Entries kept per open-ended list (category tree levels, permissions, target sites), largest first. Default 10; `truncated` reports what was cut.

tools.name: get_credit_balance
tools.description: Report your remaining Extenshi credits — for checking whether a large request fits the balance before running it. Returns every credit pool of the signed-in Extenshi account: `read` (spent one-per-call by search_extensions / get_extension / get_reviews / market_overview / get_risk_by_store_ids — the last one covers up to 40 extensions for that single credit; get_security costs 3) and `scan` (spent by scan_extension), plus `icon` and `inventory`. Each pool reports `remaining` — the number that actually gates calls (one-time free grant + purchased credits) — and `freeRemaining` (how much of the one-time, non-renewing signup grant is left). FREE to call: checking the balance spends no credit. Fetching N extensions takes read.remaining ≥ N (≥ 3N with get_security on each).

tools.name: get_approval
tools.description: Report where a proposed change stands (any pending_approval response: the hosted connector’s proposals, and request_license_terms_publication on any connection): pending (waiting for the owner in Dojo), applying, applied, rejected, failed, expired or superseded, with a one-line summary and, once applied, the outcome. Takes the approvalId from a pending_approval response. Approving happens only in Dojo, by the owner; this tool only reads. FREE — spends no credit.

tools.name: list_my_projects
tools.description: List the extension projects owned by the signed-in Extenshi account — the developer's own workspaces on extenshi.io. Returns id, name, status, target browsers, the bound GitHub repo (if any) and the claimed store listing (if any). Applies when the developer refers to "my extension" or "my project": the returned id is what get_project_state takes. `storeListings` is where each project is listed per store (planned / submitted / live — set_store_listing records it). FREE — reading your own projects spends no credit.

tools.name: get_project_state
tools.description: Read one of the developer's own projects as state you can build from: the extension TYPES they picked (popup / side panel / page enhancer / in-page assistant), the required permissions those types force, the exact manifest.json the project produces for each target browser, the files that type needs, live hosted URLs (uninstall survey), and an index of every saved tool state with its size. It reflects the site configuration at the time of the call; later changes on the site appear in a later read. The additive workspace envelope holds revisioned local observations separately from these scaffold drafts; its `document.storeListings` is where the project is listed per store (status planned / submitted / live, url, itemId, Edge productId; set_store_listing records it). It also returns the integration contract: `integration.file` is the exact content for `integration.path` that wires the extension to this project. Those bytes carry a fingerprint extenshi.io uses to tell the developer's edits from its own; a reassembled equivalent file lacks it, and the site then stops managing the values in it. `integration.unwired` lists the links this project has not set up yet (no URLs exist for them). Tool-state payloads are NOT inlined by default (a single row can be 256 KiB); includeToolStates selects which keys to inline. Manifests come as summaries by default (version, top-level keys, size, digest, origin imported/generated, and which keys of each drafted manifest differ from the imported source/built one); pass manifests "full" for the bodies, or get_project_scaffold for one browser's manifest file. `staleNames` is null until the project is renamed; after a rename it lists the earlier names (`earlierNames`), every hosted field that still holds one (`mentions`, at most 20, each with the tool that fixes it; `total`, `truncated`) and a `warning` sentence — find_brand_mentions with those names returns them all. License terms and Pay offers are searched only with pay.read (otherwise listed in `skipped`). `localization` is every server-side translation the project still lacks: {defaultLocale, locales, complete, missing, outdated, next, surfaces [{kind (pay_offers | license_terms | privacy_policy | hosted_page | landing_page), name, missing, outdated, locales [{locale, total, missing, outdated}], fixWith {read, write, args}}]}; `next` is one sentence naming the largest gap and its tools. Pay surfaces need pay.read (otherwise `skipped`); the extension's own _locales files are not part of it (localize_workflow covers those). FREE — spends no credit. Type definitions are in list_extension_templates. On this local server the answer also carries `buildMap` {running, url (while running), offered, declined, offers, home} for projectDir: the author’s build map (npx @extenshi/cli map), one per project for every agent and git worktree; absent when the directory cannot be read.

projectDir.description: The extension project's directory on this machine, absolute or relative to this server's working directory (default: the working directory). In a linked git worktree, buildMap describes the map of the main checkout, which every agent and worktree of the project shares.

includeToolStates.description: Tool keys whose saved payload to inline, e.g. ["manifest-generator", "privacy-policy-generator"]. When omitted, only the index is returned.

manifests.description: "summary" (default): each manifest as version, keys, size and digest — the same digest release.manifestDigest (built) and release.sourceManifestDigest (source) carry. "full": the drafted manifests and the imported source/built manifests in full (can be ~60 KB).

tools.name: get_project_scaffold
tools.description: The starter extension one of the developer's own projects produces, as FILES ready to write: manifest.json for the target browser, the background worker, the panel or content-script files that project's types need, placeholder icons, and src/extenshi.config.js. The config carries a fingerprint that lets extenshi.io recognise the repository as this project's; a hand-rebuilt config lacks it, and the site then stops managing those values. Intended for a NEW extension: it is a complete starter set whose files would replace same-named files in an existing repository. It is the same file set the site commits. One browser per call (default: the project's first target). FREE — spends no credit.

browser.description: Target browser; defaults to the project's first declared target.

tools.name: list_privacy_policy_versions
tools.description: List hosted privacy-policy versions for one of the developer's Pro projects: version number, kind (generated / edited / ai_updated / reverted), and which one is live. The public URL is in get_project_state hostedArtifacts.privacyPolicy. Pro only — a free project returns PROJECT_PREMIUM_REQUIRED. Does not spend a credit.

tools.name: get_privacy_policy_version
tools.description: Read the markdown (and HTML) of one hosted privacy-policy version; version numbers come from list_privacy_policy_versions. Pro only. Does not spend a credit.

tools.name: publish_privacy_policy
tools.description: Publish a hosted privacy policy for a Pro project. Changes the live public policy page. Without bodyMarkdown it generates the policy from the saved form and manifest (the first version is produced this way); with bodyMarkdown it publishes that edited (or AI-updated) draft at the same public URL. Once published, PRIVACY_POLICY_URL in the integration.file from get_project_state is the hosted URL. Pro only. With this connection’s API key the new version goes live at once, without the owner’s approval; only the hosted connector (OAuth) stores it as a proposal. The CLI command `extenshi privacy publish <file.md>` sends a file’s exact bytes and checks the stored text against it. `followUps` [{tool, readFirst, args, reason}] names the translations the new version leaves missing or outdated (set_legal_translations).

bodyMarkdown.description: Full policy markdown. When omitted, the policy is generated from the saved form and manifest.

kind.description: How this version was produced. Default: generated if no markdown, edited if markdown is set.

tools.name: update_privacy_policy_with_ai
tools.description: Propose an updated privacy policy that keeps the author's custom wording and adds sections required by new permissions or data practices. Returns proposedMarkdown only; nothing goes live. aiStep states whether the AI step ran (ran | did_not_run | discarded | not_needed) and notice says why; unless aiStep is ran, proposedMarkdown is a deterministic section merge, not an AI draft. conflictHeadings and missingCategories list what still needs a manual edit. Publishing is a separate step (publish_privacy_policy with the returned kind). Requires a policy that is already published. Pro only.

annotations.title: Update a privacy policy with AI

tools.name: get_development_guide
tools.description: For extension-development tasks: returns the complete tool inventory for THIS connection, the Extenshi service directory with access requirements and docs links, GitHub/code placement guidance, and the ordered workflow from idea and repository through implementation, assets, privacy, tests/CI, store submission and maintenance, plus store media: the scenes.json format for CLI screenshots (per-locale store screenshots) and listing artwork sizes per store. Distinguishes MCP tools from cabinet, CLI and external steps. Free; no key, account lookup or network request.

sections.description: Full guide sections to include: tools, localActions, services, repository, workflow, handoff, storeMedia, or all. Omitted: a compact overview with tool names, workflow stages and a table of contents.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the official Extenshi documentation (docs.extenshi.io) — product guides plus the full @extenshi/cli command reference (scan, review-risk, publish, login). Applies to "how do I…" questions and to exact CLI commands and flags. Free: reads public docs, no API key or quota required. Without a query it lists every available documentation page.

query.description: What to look up, e.g. "scan a zip in CI", "review-risk flags", "publish to edge", "get an API key". When omitted, every page is listed.

limit.description: Max documentation passages (page subsections) to return (1–10).

max_chars.description: Max characters per passage excerpt (200–8000, default 1500). Longer passages are cut with a link to the full page.

tools.name: localize_workflow
tools.description: Get the FREE local browser-extension localization workflow: prepare missing or stale _locales messages, translate with your own coding agent, apply validated translations and check placeholders, protected terms and listing risks. Returns commands and the JSON handoff contract. Static guidance only: no API key, network or Extenshi credits; translation uses your agent provider. Includes release availability and human review gates. Covers only the local _locales files: text stored on Extenshi (Pay offers, license terms, privacy policy, hosted pages, landing page) is listed in get_project_state `localization`.

tools.name: generate_icon_workflow
tools.description: Get the recommended FREE local workflow for creating a browser-extension icon: the agent draws the SVG itself, then `@extenshi/cli icon preview` renders an offline verification page (Chrome/Firefox/Edge toolbar mockups, palette switcher with contrast warnings, store-size matrix, PNG/ZIP export). Returns the icon design requirements (sizes, 16px legibility rules, light/dark survival) and exact commands. Static content: no API key, no network, no credits.

extension_name.description: Extension display name to inline into the preview command (optional).

tools.name: generate_welcome_page_workflow
tools.description: Get the design brief for a browser-extension welcome page — the page a user lands on right after installing. Returns the one action the page is built to drive (pin the extension, keep the new-tab change, use it on a site), exactly which illustrations to produce for that goal, how to capture and crop them, how to place numbered/arrow markers showing where to click, the limits enforced on save, and the block JSON format. Store screenshots Extenshi already hosts (from get_extension) can serve as illustrations. Static content: no API key, no network, no credits.

goal.description: The single action the page drives. PIN_EXTENSION (default) fits ~90% of extensions; NEW_TAB_OPT_IN for new-tab replacements; VISIT_SITE when the extension injects a widget into a site.

what_it_does.description: One or two sentences on what the extension actually does.

target_site.description: For VISIT_SITE: the site the extension injects into, e.g. youtube.com.

store_screenshots.description: Screenshot URLs from get_extension. Offered to the agent as ready-made illustration material that needs no upload.

existing_steps.description: Steps the author already wrote, so the brief adds visuals instead of rewriting.

accent_color.description: The page's accent colour as hex, so drawn illustrations match it.

tools.name: generate_pin_guide
tools.description: Get the illustrated "pin the extension to the toolbar" steps for Chrome, Edge and Firefox as an offline kit for a welcome page bundled INSIDE the extension: SVGs with the extension icon and numbered markers drawn in, an HTML fragment that passes the extension CSP, captions in 11 languages as chrome.i18n messages, and an ES module that picks the user's browser and reads whether the icon is already pinned (action.getUserSettings().isOnToolbar). The default `part` is a short overview with sizes; `html`, `messages`, `script` and `css` return the parts, narrowed by `browsers` / `locales`. `npx @extenshi/cli pin-guide` writes the same kit to disk. Static content: no API key, no network, no credits.

extension_name.description: Extension display name, drawn into the menu rows.

part.description: overview (default), html, messages, script or css.

locales.description: BCP 47 tags: en, es, pt-BR, fr, de, it, ru, ja, ko, zh-CN, ar. Default: all. English is added to any selection — it is the fallback text inside the HTML.

theme.description: light (default), dark, or auto — a light and a dark copy switched by CSS.

icon_href.description: The icon as the page will load it: a path inside the extension package relative to the page (e.g. ../icons/icon-48.png), or a data:image/png|jpeg|webp|svg+xml;base64 URI. Remote URLs are refused — the page has to work offline.

accent_color.description: Marker and highlight colour as hex.

key_prefix.description: Prefix of the chrome.i18n message names (default pinGuide).

tools.name: generate_landing_page
tools.description: Generate a static landing page (homepage) for a browser extension as one self-contained HTML file: no JavaScript, escaped text, http(s)-only links (the support link may also be a mailto: address), and store buttons only for the store URLs given. Same generator as the cabinet Page generator, so a saved `page-generator` form from get_project_state maps field for field. Optional logo (inline SVG, validated and embedded as an image, or an image URL), screenshots and the canonical homepage URL for Open Graph and JSON-LD. Returns JSON {html, bytes, warnings, nextSteps}: warnings list input that was dropped or clamped; nextSteps cover hosting the file on HTTPS and registering the URL with upsert_hosted_page, which feeds HOMEPAGE_URL. Extenshi does not host the page. With schemaVersion 2 the page is built from sections, theme tokens, SEO and locales (see the field descriptions); the result adds problems [{path, severity, message, fix}] and localePages. Static content: no API key, no network, no credits.

description.description: Short paragraph on what the extension does; also the meta description.

accentColor.description: Hex accent colour for the primary button and monogram (default #5e5ce6).

chromeUrl.description: Chrome Web Store listing URL. Empty or omitted hides the Chrome button.

firefoxUrl.description: Firefox Add-ons listing URL. Empty or omitted hides the Firefox button.

edgeUrl.description: Edge Add-ons listing URL. Empty or omitted hides the Edge button.

privacyPolicyUrl.description: Privacy policy URL for the footer (for example the hosted privacy.extenshi.io page).

supportUrl.description: Support link for the footer: an http(s) URL, or a single mailto: address (optionally ?subject= with a percent-encoded value).

homepageUrl.description: Public https URL the page will be served from: canonical link, og:url, JSON-LD url, and the base for relative screenshot paths in og:image.

features.description: Feature cards; entries with an empty title are skipped.

screenshots.description: Screenshots as https URLs (for example store screenshots from get_extension) or paths relative to index.html, each with alt text.

logoSvg.description: Inline SVG logo source. Refused (monogram shown, reason in warnings) if it contains scripts, event handlers, foreignObject, animation, entity references or non-fragment hrefs.

logoUrl.description: Logo image as an https URL, a relative path, or a data:image/(png|jpeg|gif|webp);base64 URL.

schemaVersion.description: 2 builds a full homepage from sections, theme tokens, SEO and locales. Absent: the classic one-screen page (unchanged output). draft_landing_page returns a complete v2 form.

id.description: Lowercase slug, unique; also the locale override key.

hidden.description: Keep in the form, leave out of the page.

sections.description: Ordered page sections (v2). Fields per type: hero {headline?, subheadline?, showBadges?}; about {body — plain text, blank line = new paragraph}; features {items: [{title, description?}]}; screenshots {items: [{url, alt, caption?}]} (hosted: upload_project_media URLs or store screenshots); how-it-works {steps: [{title, description?}]}; pricing {plans: [{name?, price?, period? one-time|month|year|lifetime, description?, features?, highlighted?, offerSku?, ctaLabel?, ctaUrl?}], note?} — offerSku binds the plan to the project's Extenshi Pay offer so price and period come from the live offer; faq {items: [{question, answer}]} (also emitted as FAQPage JSON-LD); testimonials {items: [{quote, author, role?, sourceUrl, sourceLabel?}]} — real, attributed quotes only: author and a public https sourceUrl are required; store-badges {browsers?: [chrome|firefox|edge]}; changelog {entries: [{version, date? YYYY-MM-DD, notes: [string]}]}; links {items?: [{label, url}], includeProjectLinks?}. Plain text only everywhere — no HTML, no scripts.

tokens.description: Theme tokens (v2): hex colours per mode and fonts from a system-font allowlist (no web fonts — the hosted CSP loads nothing external). Poor contrast is reported as a warning.

seo.description: SEO / Open Graph (v2): <title>, meta description, og:image, twitter:site, JSON-LD author.

defaultLocale.description: Locale of the base content (default en).

locales.description: Translations (v2), keyed by locale (de, pt-BR or the _locales spelling pt_BR; hosted pages accept store locales). Each is served at {url}/{locale} with hreflang alternates. sections.{id} mirrors that section's shape; only strings are taken (arrays merge by index), so a translation cannot change structure. ui overrides built-in headings and button labels.

ui.description: Built-in strings to override (v2): addToChrome, getForFirefox, getForEdge, screenshots, features, howItWorks, pricing, faq, testimonials, storeBadges, changelog, links, privacy, support, feedback, terms, install, popular, perMonth, perYear, oneTime, lifetime, source, languages, logoAlt.

uninstallUrl.description: Hosted uninstall feedback form URL (footer, v2).

tools.name: list_extension_templates
tools.description: The kinds of browser extension you can build, with the permissions each one REQUIRES: Popup (toolbar window), Side panel (docked beside the page), Page enhancer (runs on sites you list), In-page assistant (your own UI over any site). Types combine, and the required permissions are the union. Applies when choosing manifest permissions: it gives the minimum each shape needs (store review flags padded permissions). Also states the cross-browser rules (Chromium side_panel vs Firefox sidebar_action) and the rule that a manifest may not name a file the package lacks. FREE: no API key, no quota. A specific project's chosen types are in get_project_state.

types.description: Type ids to include (popup, sidepanel, content, overlay); all four when omitted.

tools.name: scan_extension
tools.description: Run a pre-publish security scan on a local extension artifact (.zip/.crx/.xpi) and return the report. Uses one scan from your one-time free allowance (3 scans) or a purchased scan credit once that runs out. Streams live per-scanner progress.

artifact_path.description: Absolute or relative path to the built extension artifact (≤50 MB).

extension_id.description: Optional numeric catalog ID to associate this scan with a catalog listing.

store_id.description: Optional: associate this scan with a catalog listing by its store id (the id in the store URL; add `store` for a Chrome/Edge id).

store.description: Which store `store_id` belongs to. REQUIRED for Chrome/Edge ids (identical format).

tools.name: get_build_map
tools.description: The author’s build map of the extension project in projectDir (npx @extenshi/cli map): progress, the steps waiting on the author (needsYou), the steps that can start now (next, safe to run in parallel), who works on what, every step with the task it is on, and the variants offered to the author with their answer (reviews: waiting, picked, or redo with what to change). skills lists the published agent skills with the instructions for the steps not done yet (steps: step id → skill names; index: name → what it teaches and the url of its SKILL.md): load a step’s skills before working on it. One map per project, shared by every agent and git worktree. While the author’s map runs, the answer carries the project facts and the release the map runs (map); update, when present, says what to do because the map draws older or newer steps than this server knows, or a newer release is out. Otherwise facts is false and steps proven only by project files look not done. Free; local files only.

projectDir.description: The extension project's directory on this machine, absolute or relative to this server's working directory (default: the working directory). In a linked git worktree, buildMap describes the map of the main checkout, which every agent and worktree of the project shares.

tools.name: show_build_map
tools.description: Show the author the build map in the conversation (clients that show MCP Apps, such as Claude, draw it inline; elsewhere the answer has the link to the author’s map). Pass `step` to open one step, such as the variants waiting on the author after request_build_review: the author picks one, asks for another round, marks their own tasks or skips a step right there, and get_build_map reads the answer. Call it when the author should look or choose; to read the map yourself use get_build_map, which draws nothing. Free; local files only.

projectDir.description: The extension project's directory on this machine, absolute or relative to this server's working directory (default: the working directory). In a linked git worktree, buildMap describes the map of the main checkout, which every agent and worktree of the project shares.

step.description: The build step id, as get_build_map lists them (iconConcepts, screenshots, listing, …).

tools.name: report_build_step
tools.description: Report on a build map step as an agent. state: start (you are on it; the answer names the step’s skills, the published instructions to load before the work), progress (with progress 0–1), done (closes the current task, or `task`; `files` are hashed into the evidence journal as proof) or stop. A step whose inputs are not done is refused while the author’s map runs. The author’s choice between variants is not closed by `done`: pass `choice` (the variant id the author picked in the chat) or `redo` (what to change, in the author’s words) to record the author’s answer. Never record a choice the author did not make. Free; writes .extenshi/build-map.json in the project.

projectDir.description: The extension project's directory on this machine, absolute or relative to this server's working directory (default: the working directory). In a linked git worktree, buildMap describes the map of the main checkout, which every agent and worktree of the project shares.

step.description: The build step id, as get_build_map lists them (iconConcepts, screenshots, listing, …).

agent.description: Who works on the step, shown to the author on the map: a short label such as "icons agent".

task.description: The task `done` closes, counted from 0 (default: the current one).

progress.description: How far the current task is (state progress).

claim.description: What the closed task produced, in one line (default: the task).

files.description: Files that show the task done, relative to projectDir: hashed, so the entry is checked.

urls.description: Pages that show the task done.

choice.description: The variant id the author picked in the chat.

redo.description: What to change, in the author’s words: asks for another round.

round.description: The round the author answered (refused if another one is open).

tools.name: request_build_review
tools.description: Offer the author variants to choose from on the build map: icon concepts (iconConcepts), screenshots (screenshots) or listing copy (listing). Each variant is a preview page or image inside the project (an `npx @extenshi/cli icon preview` page fits icons) or an https address; `image` adds a thumbnail. The step waits on the author until they pick one or ask for another round. Returns the link to the step while the map runs: give it to the author, then read the answer with get_build_map. Free; local files only.

projectDir.description: The extension project's directory on this machine, absolute or relative to this server's working directory (default: the working directory). In a linked git worktree, buildMap describes the map of the main checkout, which every agent and worktree of the project shares.

step.description: The build step id, as get_build_map lists them (iconConcepts, screenshots, listing, …).

agent.description: Who works on the step, shown to the author on the map: a short label such as "icons agent".

preview.description: A preview page or image inside the project, relative to projectDir, or an https address.

image.description: A thumbnail image for the map, like preview.

tools.name: publish_extension
tools.description: Publish an extension artifact (.zip/.crx/.xpi) to Chrome Web Store, Firefox AMO, and/or Edge Add-ons: uploads and submits a new version to each selected store. FREE and fully local: the upload goes from this machine straight to the store APIs using store credentials from the MCP server environment (CHROME_APP_ID/CHROME_PUBLISHER_ID/CHROME_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY, FIREFOX_ADDON_GUID/FIREFOX_JWT_ISSUER/FIREFOX_JWT_SECRET, EDGE_PRODUCT_ID/EDGE_CLIENT_ID/EDGE_API_KEY). Chrome uses the author's own service account (Chrome Web Store API V2), which updates existing items only. The upload itself is local, but publishing is in an active testing phase: a quick Extenshi access check runs first (it identifies your account by EXTENSHI_API_KEY). Edge submissions are polled to a terminal status. For Firefox, listing_path turns the upload into a listed AMO submission with metadata: first-time add-on creation (gated by allow_new_addon or the project decision), per-locale name/summary/description, categories, license, homepage, support email and URL, privacy policy, release and reviewer notes, reviewer source (source_path) and previews (screenshots_dir); the result lists each step. source_path without listing_path updates an existing AMO add-on: the version is created with release_notes and reviewer_notes, the source archive is uploaded to it, and the listing stays as it is. The artifact is not security-scanned by this tool (scanning is scan_extension).

artifact_path.description: Path to the packaged extension (.zip for Chrome/Edge, .xpi/.zip for Firefox).

stores.description: Target stores; defaults to every store that has complete credentials in the environment.

firefox_artifact_path.description: Separate Firefox artifact (.xpi); defaults to artifact_path.

release_notes.description: Firefox: the new version's public release notes on AMO (en-US; an AMO listing's own release notes win). Edge: sent as the notes for certification, which only reviewers see, unless reviewer_notes is given. Chrome: not sent (the Chrome Web Store API has no such field).

reviewer_notes.description: Notes for store reviewers only, not shown publicly. Firefox: the version's AMO approval notes, at most 3,000 characters (an AMO listing's own reviewer notes win). Edge: the notes for certification, in place of release_notes. Chrome: not sent.

listing_path.description: Firefox: AMO listing file (JSON with per-locale fields, or the AMO.md that generate-listing --store firefox writes, placeholders filled). Makes the Firefox submission a listed one with metadata: the add-on is created on first submission (see allow_new_addon) or its listing is edited, then privacy policy, release notes, reviewer notes, source and previews are applied.

source_path.description: Firefox: reviewer source archive (.zip/.tar.gz/.tgz/.tar.bz2), uploaded to the new version after it is created. With listing_path it is part of the listed submission. Without listing_path it updates an add-on that already exists on AMO: the version is created with release_notes and reviewer_notes, the archive is uploaded to it, and the listing is not read or changed.

screenshots_dir.description: Firefox: AMO previews in file-name order: a directory of .png/.jpg/.gif files, or the extenshi screenshots output directory (its firefox/<locale>/ set, default locale first). Needs listing_path.

allow_new_addon.description: Firefox: permits creating a NEW AMO add-on, whose id becomes permanent. With project_id the project's decided amo.addonId governs creation instead.

addon_id.description: Firefox: the AMO add-on id ({GUID} or name@domain), stated explicitly. Needed with allow_new_addon when there is no project_id; fills FIREFOX_ADDON_GUID when the environment has none.

replace_screenshots.description: Firefox: replaces the previews of an existing AMO add-on with screenshots_dir.

project_id.description: Dojo project id. Its owner-decided amo.addonId gates first-time AMO creation and has to equal FIREFOX_ADDON_GUID.

extension_id.description: Numeric catalog ID — checks publish-beta access against this specific extension.

validate_only.description: Only check which store credentials are configured and valid; publish nothing.

tools.name: build_map_view
tools.description: The build map page reads its snapshot. Called by the page only.

annotations.title: Build map: read for the page

tools.name: build_map_answer
tools.description: The author answers on the build map page: marks a task, does a step themselves or skips it, picks a variant or asks for another round. Called by the page only, when the author clicks.

tools.name: build_map_file
tools.description: The build map page loads a variant thumbnail. Called by the page only.

instructions: Extenshi covers browser-extension development and operations: catalog and security data on other people's extensions, and the signed-in developer's own projects, hosted pages, Pay applications and privacy policy. get_development_guide (free) returns the workflow, this connection's tools, services and documentation links; search_docs (free) returns current documentation and exact CLI flags. get_credit_balance reports the remaining credits; get_risk_by_store_ids covers 40 store IDs per read, and get_security costs three reads. list_my_projects returns the developer's projects (create_project adds one); get_project_state returns a project's configuration, including integration.file (the content for integration.path that links a repository to the project) and integration.unwired. The build map (npx @extenshi/cli map) is one local page per project and its worktrees, where the author follows progress and makes choices. get_decisions lists owner decisions (AMO add-on id, license, seller, pricing); propose_decision proposes a value, and the owner decides it in Dojo. Pay applications are separate from projects (list_pay_apps, create_pay_app, get_pay_readiness) and need the pay.read / pay.write scopes; agreement and KYC happen in the browser, and only the publishable SDK key and the public verification key belong in extension code. Hosted privacy-policy tools need a Pro project: publish_privacy_policy updates the live public page; update_privacy_policy_with_ai only proposes. Registered tools prove neither account entitlements nor a completed release. This connection exposes scan_extension and publish_extension for local artifacts; they need credentials and publishing access. With an API key, payment, policy-publish and legal-translation changes apply at once; the hosted connector proposes them instead. API keys for the local package: https://dojo.extenshi.io/api-keys.
